summary.summary: Gloucestershire's borrowing rose £31.1m to £259.5m in 2025/26 (average cost 4.43%), driven by £56.1m of new market borrowing including seven temporary LA-to-LA loans at 4.15%-4.7% taken to manage liquidity; the CFR rose to £497.9m. Investments fell £8m to £193.4m, and the council states plainly that balances and reserves are reducing because of internal borrowing on the capital programme and the increasing SEND deficit - though no deficit figure is given in this report. Nearly half the portfolio (£90m principal, market value £86.6m) sits in long-dated strategic pooled funds protected by a statutory override extended to 31 March 2029; within these, a social housing REIT has fallen to £3.2m from £5m invested, with the valuer citing distressed housing associations in the sector. Three Dexia LOBOs (£22.05m) saw an increased probability of lender calls as rates rose, but none were called. All activity complied with the strategy and prudential indicators.

signals.headline: Borrowing up from £228.4m to £259.5m in 2025/26 (£56.1m new, including £50m of temporary LA loans outstanding at year end, all maturing May 2026-February 2027); CFR up to £497.9m
signals.why: The council is rolling short-term debt for liquidity, so £50m must be refinanced within 12 months in a market where year-end LA rates reached 5-7%.

signals.headline: Increasing SEND deficit named alongside capital internal borrowing as the cause of reducing balances and reserves; no deficit figure stated in this report
signals.why: The schools deficit is draining the cash that currently substitutes for external borrowing, bringing forward real borrowing need.

signals.headline: £22.05m of LOBOs across three Dexia loans; increased probability of call options being exercised as rates rose in 2025/26, though none were called
signals.why: A Dexia call would force repayment or refinancing at rates above the 4.35% the loans currently cost.

news_drafts.headline: Gloucestershire general reserves at £36.3m face further erosion as day-to-day spending overshoots budget by £2.4m amid school and care cost pressures
news_drafts.lead: Gloucestershire County Council's general reserves, already at its minimum safety level, face further erosion this year as day-to-day spending overshoots budget by £2.4m. The Corporate Overview and Scrutiny Committee heard that reserves stand at £36.3m, only just above the 5% minimum the council has set. The pressure comes from two unbudgeted demand surges: a schools funding shortfall that has grown by £14m in three months to £68.4m as more children enter special education, and adult social care overspending by £3.2m on learning disabilities packages. Children's disability placements add another £1.8m pressure. The council has deferred £39.8m of its capital programme—including £17.6m of children's services schemes and £11.1m of transport work—to ease immediate cash strain. A £7m portion of its £37.2m savings plan also faces delivery risk. The schools deficit depends on government approval of the council's special educational needs reform plan to unlock a grant covering 90% of costs, expected in autumn.

news_drafts.headline: Gloucestershire pension fund completed £2.74m investment transition to 152% funding but faced 16-month staffing shortage resolved by March 2027
news_drafts.lead: Gloucestershire's pension fund has completed its transition to new investment managers at a cost of £2.74 million, representing 0.13% of the £2.04 billion in assets moved from Brunel Pensions Partnership to LGPS Central by 1 April 2026. The fund remains strongly funded at 152%, with assets exceeding liabilities significantly. However, the Pension Committee heard that administration staffing has been insufficient for 16 months, with the fund unable to deliver services effectively due to recruitment and retention difficulties. Data quality issues affecting member, employer and payroll records have persisted for five months. Both problems are expected to be resolved by March 2027. The committee was also told that control deficiencies identified in 2020/21 audits remain outstanding at year-end 2026, though the new cloud-based system implemented in April should address segregation-of-duties and journal-approval weaknesses.
news_drafts.paper_title: Agenda Item 6 - Pension Fund Audit & Financial Statements 2025-26 - Appendix 1 - Draft Audit Findings Report

news_drafts.headline: Gloucestershire pays care providers without signed contracts in place
news_drafts.lead: Gloucestershire County Council has identified significant gaps in its management of adult social care provider contracts. An audit of care homes, nursing homes and domiciliary care providers found that 34% of home care contracts and 68% of residential and nursing care contracts had not been formally accepted, despite the council continuing to make payments. The council has no centrally maintained contracts register and lacks agreed policies and procedures for contract management. The audit raised three high-priority and four medium-priority recommendations. The findings mean the council cannot fully verify that payments are supported by valid documentation or that agreed terms are in place.

findings.headline: Capital programme reprofiled down by £39.8m, deferring delivery of originally approved schemes
findings.detail: The capital programme approved in February 2026 was £224.054m. After review of delivery schedules and priorities, this has been revised to £184.251m—a reduction of £39.803m. Major deferrals include £17.6m of children's services schemes, £11.1m of transport and highways, and £4.8m of community safety (fire appliances and Cinderford Fire Station). These represent delivery delays extending the financing requirement into future years.
findings.matters: Large-scale capital deferrals indicate the council's original capital plans are not achievable on the scheduled timetable, extending the financing tail and signalling delivery or funding constraints.
findings.figures: £224.054m original budget, £184.251m revised budget, £39.803m deferred (17.8% of original)
findings.quote: The capital programme budget approved as part of MTFS in February 2026 was £224.054 million. Following the review of project delivery schedules and programme priorities, the proposed revised programme profile is £184.251 million.

findings.headline: Savings programme at significant risk with £7.7m of £37.2m (21%) in amber or red categories
findings.detail: Of the £37.169m savings target, only £29.449m (79%) is on track. £7.029m is at moderate risk and £691k at significant risk. At-risk schemes include ASC residential deregistrations (£200k), Sensory Services (£50k), Corporate Resources SAP licensing (£191k), and corporate estate reshaping (£250k). If these do not materialise as planned, the current £2.4m overspend will be compounded.
findings.matters: Savings delivery failure compounds the revenue overspend risk. Both issues occurring together would force significant reserve drawdown and breach minimum reserve levels.
findings.figures: £37.169m total savings target, £29.449m (79%) on track, £7.029m (19%) amber risk, £691k (2%) red risk
findings.quote: As at Quarter 1, £29.449 million (79.23%) is on target to be achieved in year, with £7.029 million (18.91%) being a moderate (amber) risk and £691k (1.86%) being at significant risk.

findings.headline: Children's disability placements and allowances overrunning by £2.2m
findings.detail: Children & Families is forecasting an overspend of £1.128m, with disabled children's care packages at £1.766m and Special Guardianship allowances at £407k overspending. These are partially offset by underspends in Safeguarding staff (£1.057m from lower agency costs) and Education Commissioning (£277k from vacancies). The underlying demand pressure in placements is being masked by operational cost controls.
findings.matters: Like ASC, this is demand-led. The need to cut agency staffing and accept vacancies to offset placement growth indicates the council is running tighter operationally just to fund increasing caseload costs.
findings.figures: £1.128m total overspend, £1.766m disabled children's packages, £407k Special Guardianship allowances
findings.quote: Disabled Children's care packages are forecast to overspend by £1.766 million based on current numbers of young people supported but allowing for those reaching 18, new packages and additional support through holiday periods

findings.headline: Adult Social Care Learning Disabilities overrunning by £3.2m due to unbudgeted demographic growth
findings.detail: Adult Social Care is overspending by £3.864m total, with £3.2m of this driven by Learning Disabilities external care packages. The council identifies 'higher than anticipated demographic growth' as the cause, indicating the budget was set on inadequate assumptions about population growth of adults requiring external care. This is a structural demand-led overspend rather than operational inefficiency.
findings.matters: Demographic-driven social care overspends are difficult to recover in-year and signal underlying budget-setting problems. Persistent pressures of this type become unsustainable without service restrictions or income changes.
findings.figures: £3.2m Learning Disabilities overspend within £3.864m total ASC overspend
findings.quote: The overspend is driven by external care, largely Learning Disabilities (LD) which is forecasting a £3.2 million overspend. Higher than anticipated demographic growth is resulting in pressures across external care budgets

findings.headline: DSG deficit grown by £14m in one quarter and now contingent on government grant approval to avoid serious pressure
findings.detail: The Dedicated Schools Grant deficit has deteriorated from the £54.408m budgeted in February to £68.447m forecast, an increase of £14.039m driven by higher than expected EHCP numbers and special school placement demand. The cumulative DSG deficit is now £193.165m. This excludes the High Needs Stability Grant (90% government funding) expected in Autumn 2026, which requires approval of the council's SEND Reform Plan. If the grant does not materialise or is delayed, the council faces an unbudgeted £14m pressure.
findings.matters: The £193m cumulative deficit is a material contingent liability. The council's financial position depends materially on receipt of a government grant whose approval is not yet confirmed.
findings.figures: £68.447m in-year DSG deficit (budgeted £54.408m), £14.039m deterioration, £193.165m cumulative deficit, government grant 90% of deficit pending SEND Plan approval
findings.quote: the in-year DSG deficit is now forecast to be £68.447 million, which is £14.039 million higher than the figure projected in the MTFS. The cumulative DSG deficit is therefore forecast to reach £193.165 million as at 31 March 2027. These figures do not include any impact of the High Needs Stability Grant (90% funding commitment from Central Government), of which the first instalments are expected in Autumn 2026, assuming the SEND Reform Plan is approved.
